COAD.description: Colon adenocarcinoma. encode_chromatin added 2026-09-03 (expanded-covariate-sources task, Objective A.4): adult primary colonic mucosa DNase-seq, filling the open-chromatin gap alongside the existing TCGA ATAC coverage (a matched-tissue, non-tumor complement to the TCGA-tumor ATAC signal). encode_chromatin cell lines added 2026-09-07 (Martincorena et al. 2017 STAR Methods confirms dNdScv's matrix used Roadmap cell lines, prompting this search): HCT116, Caco-2, LoVo, SW480, HT-29, RKO -- six independent colon-cancer cell lines with native-GRCh38 ENCODE tracks, complementing the existing adult primary colonic mucosa DNase-seq. HCT116 is also this project's one existing Repli-seq source (GSE137764/MAT), so this reuses an already-vetted colon-cancer line rather than introducing a new one, plus five more independent colon lines.

BRCA.description: Breast invasive carcinoma. encode_chromatin added 2026-09-03 (expanded-covariate-sources task, Objective A.4): adult primary breast epithelium DNase-seq, filling the open-chromatin gap alongside the existing TCGA ATAC coverage. encode_chromatin cell lines added 2026-09-07: Martincorena et al. 2017's own STAR Methods (the primary dNdScv paper, not just the package/GitHub repo) confirms their 20-PC matrix was built from 63 Roadmap cell lines, not primary tissue -- a gap this registry hadn't checked before. Added MCF-7 (mammary gland adenocarcinoma, ENCODE's own native-GRCh38 ChIP-seq/DNase, 8/8 marks) and T47D (breast ductal carcinoma, DNase only), both real breast-cancer cell lines, complementing the existing adult primary breast epithelium DNase-seq rather than replacing it.

UCEC.description: Uterine Corpus Endometrial Carcinoma. encode_chromatin added 2026-09-03 (expanded-covariate-sources task): ENCODE has adult primary uterus tissue for 5 of our 7 default marks plus DNase -- H3K4me1, H3K9me3, H3K36me3, H3K27ac, H3K27me3 and DNase (one of two available adult uterus DNase experiments used). Missing H3K4me3 and H3K9ac (not released for this biosample). encode_chromatin cell line added 2026-09-07: Ishikawa (DNase-seq, native GRCh38) is a genuine endometrial adenocarcinoma cell line -- a disease-matched complement to the adult primary uterus tissue tracks above, not just an organ-level proxy. Found via Martincorena et al. 2017's STAR Methods confirming dNdScv's matrix is cell-line-based.

STAD.description: Stomach Adenocarcinoma. encode_chromatin added 2026-09-03 (expanded-covariate-sources task, Objective A.4): adult primary stomach tissue DNase-seq, filling the open-chromatin gap alongside the existing TCGA ATAC coverage.

TGCT.description: Testicular Germ Cell Tumors. encode_chromatin added 2026-09-03 (expanded-covariate-sources task): ENCODE has adult primary testis tissue for 6 of our 7 default marks plus DNase -- H3K4me1, H3K27ac, H3K27me3, H3K9me3, H3K36me3 and DNase all from the same 37yo donor; H3K4me3 only exists from a different (54yo) donor, used anyway since it's the only adult testis H3K4me3 available (a documented donor mismatch, not a tissue mismatch). Missing only H3K9ac. encode_chromatin cell line added 2026-09-07: NT2/D1 is a testicular embryonal carcinoma line -- a genuine TGCT-subtype cell line, not just a testis-tissue proxy -- with H3K9ac coverage, filling this cohort's one remaining mark gap (the adult primary testis tissue above is missing H3K9ac). Found via the same Martincorena et al. 2017 STAR-Methods-prompted ENCODE cell-line check as the other cohorts above. repliseq stays null, and that is a tested negative as of 2026-09-18, not an unfilled gap: H1 hESC (GSE137764 16-fraction MAT) was registered on a cell-of-origin argument and then dropped after measuring as nothing on this cohort -- held-out R^2 -0.0003 at matched n_components, ELPD within half a nat over 16852 genes, unchanged PIT calibration, and identical residual spatial autocorrelation. It also costs every chrX/chrY gene, the autosome-only MAT's standard price. No testis or germ-cell-tumor line exists in ENCODE's complete 182-experiment replication-timing catalog either.

OV.description: Ovarian Serous Cystadenocarcinoma. encode_chromatin added 2026-09-03 (expanded-covariate-sources task, Objective A.3): DNase-seq substituted for the missing TCGA ATAC-seq coverage (Corces et al. 2018 didn't profile ovarian cancer) -- adult primary ovary tissue DNase-seq exists natively on ENCODE (9 released adult experiments; one used here), unrelated to the ATAC gap since ATAC and DNase are separate assay catalogs.

SKCM.description: Skin Cutaneous Melanoma; GTEx representative column is sun-exposed skin (lower leg) since cutaneous melanoma is predominantly associated with sun-exposed body sites, not sun-shielded ones -- not-sun-exposed skin is also GTEx-mapped for the full covariate matrix. Roadmap eids are primary melanocyte cultures (E059, E061), matching melanoma's cell of origin rather than the broader skin fibroblast/keratinocyte epigenomes (E126/E127) also in the 127-panel. encode_chromatin (DNase) checked 2026-09-03 (Objective A.4) and NOT added: ENCODE's only melanocyte DNase-seq experiments are newborn foreskin or unspecified life stage (ENCSR518JGY, ENCSR434OBM, ENCSR000ELD) -- no adult sample exists, so left unfilled rather than using an age-mismatched proxy. encode_chromatin cell lines added 2026-09-07: SK-MEL-5 and COLO829 are real melanoma cell lines (DNase-seq only, native GRCh38) -- ENCODE has no adult melanocyte DNase (see above), but does have melanoma-line DNase, a different but genuinely disease-matched proxy. Found via Martincorena et al. 2017's STAR Methods confirming dNdScv's matrix is cell-line-based.

ACC.description: Adrenocortical Carcinoma. No adult adrenal/adrenocortical epigenome exists in Roadmap's 127-panel -- only E080 (Fetal Adrenal Gland), rejected as a tissue-stage mismatch, same rationale as UCEC/TGCT rejecting anatomically-close-but-wrong candidates. No adrenal/H295R cell line in ENCODE's ReplicationTimingSeries (22 series checked) or GEO GSE137764 (H1/H9/HCT116-only, confirmed). encode_chromatin added 2026-09-03 (expanded-covariate-sources task): ENCODE's own native-GRCh38 experiments cover adult primary adrenal gland tissue directly (a female, 41yo donor) for 5 of our 7 default marks plus DNase -- a source Roadmap's 127-panel never had. H3K9ac and H3K27ac have no released adult adrenal gland experiment on ENCODE (checked via the full organ_slims=adrenal+gland Histone ChIP-seq listing, not a per-mark miss); left unfilled rather than substituting a cell line.

BLCA.description: Bladder Urothelial Carcinoma. No bladder/urothelial/urinary anatomy category exists in Roadmap's standard 127-panel (checked the full EID_metadata.tab, not just a candidate shortlist). No bladder-derived cell line in ENCODE's ReplicationTimingSeries (28 series checked across both the UW 6-fraction and Gilbert wavelet cohorts) or GEO GSE137764 (H1/H9/HCT116-only, confirmed). encode_chromatin added 2026-09-03 (expanded-covariate-sources task): ENCODE has adult primary urinary bladder tissue (same male donor) for 4 of our 7 default marks -- H3K4me1, H3K27ac, H3K4me3, H3K36me3. Missing H3K9ac, H3K9me3, H3K27me3 (not released for this biosample). The only bladder DNase-seq experiment on ENCODE (ENCSR813CKU) is embryonic, not adult -- rejected as a tissue-stage mismatch, same rationale ACC/UCEC/TGCT already use for rejecting Roadmap's fetal-only candidates. encode_chromatin cell line added 2026-09-07: an ENCODE urothelium cell line (DNase-seq, native GRCh38) -- this cohort's first DNase source of any kind (the primary-tissue marks above have no matching adult bladder DNase-seq experiment). Found via Martincorena et al. 2017's STAR Methods confirming dNdScv's matrix is cell-line-based, which prompted this ENCODE classification=cell+line check.

CESC.description: Cervical Squamous Cell Carcinoma and Endocervical Adenocarcinoma. GTEx representative column is Cervix_Ectocervix (squamous epithelium) since squamous carcinoma is the majority histology in this cohort. Roadmap's only cervix entry is E117 (HeLa-S3), a cervical cancer cell line rather than primary tissue -- same rationale as using K562 for LAML, the best available match when no normal-tissue epigenome exists for this anatomy. HeLa-S3 is also in ENCODE's UW 6-fraction Repli-seq cohort, so both roadmap and repliseq use the same cell line here. encode_chromatin (DNase) checked 2026-09-03 (Objective A.4) and NOT added: ENCODE has zero cervix/ectocervix/endocervix DNase-seq experiments at all (searchTerm queries for all three return no results) -- not just no adult match, no match of any kind. encode_chromatin cell line added 2026-09-07: HeLa-S3 is already this cohort's Roadmap (E117) and Repli-seq choice (see above) -- ENCODE's own native-GRCh38 ChIP-seq/DNase experiments for the same cell line (8/8 marks, independent from Roadmap's hg19 consolidated signal) were not yet pulled in as encode_chromatin. Added now; still the best-available cervical-cancer cell-line match, same caveat as before (a cell line, not normal tissue).

CHOL.description: Cholangiocarcinoma. GTEx maps to Liver/Liver_Portal_Tract; Roadmap and repliseq both use liver-tissue/liver-cell-line sources (E066 primary liver, E118/HepG2 hepatocellular line) since no bile-duct-specific epigenome or cell line exists in either resource -- HepG2 is a hepatocyte line, not cholangiocyte, so this is the best available organ-level proxy rather than a cell-type match, same caveat pattern as CESC's HeLa-S3 use. HepG2 is also in ENCODE's UW 6-fraction Repli-seq cohort (same assay family as MCF-7/HeLa-S3), all 6 fractions present. encode_chromatin added 2026-09-03 (expanded-covariate-sources task, Objective A.4): adult primary liver tissue DNase-seq (not HepG2 -- same organ-level-proxy caveat as the marks/repliseq above, but a real tissue sample rather than a cell line where one exists for this assay). encode_chromatin cell lines added 2026-09-07: HuH-7 and HuH-7.5 (DNase-seq, native GRCh38) are hepatocellular carcinoma lines distinct from HepG2 above -- still the same organ-level (liver, not bile-duct) proxy caveat as HepG2's use in Roadmap/Repli-seq, but two independent additional liver-cancer lines' open-chromatin signal. Found via Martincorena et al. 2017's STAR Methods confirming dNdScv's matrix is cell-line-based.

DLBC.description: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. GTEx maps to Whole_Blood/Spleen (no lymph-node column in GTEx). No TCGA ATAC-seq coverage (atac: null). Roadmap uses E032 (primary B cells from peripheral blood, the direct cell-of-origin match, 6/7 marks -- H3K9ac 404s) plus E062 (primary PBMCs, broader immune mix, 7/7 marks) for fuller coverage, same two-epigenome pattern as CHOL/CESC. Repliseq uses GM12878 (EBV-transformed lymphoblastoid B-cell line), the standard ENCODE UW 6-fraction Repli-seq series, hg19, all 6 fractions live-verified -- the closest available cell-type match for a B-cell malignancy, analogous to CHOL's HepG2/BRCA's MCF-7 choices. encode_chromatin added 2026-09-03 (expanded-covariate-sources task, Objective A.3): DNase-seq substituted for the missing TCGA ATAC-seq coverage, same rationale as OV -- adult primary peripheral-blood B cell DNase-seq exists natively on ENCODE (8 released adult experiments; one used here), matching E032's cell-of-origin choice. encode_chromatin cell lines added 2026-09-07: Karpas-422, OCI-LY1, OCI-LY3, OCI-LY7 and SU-DHL-6 are actual diffuse large B-cell lymphoma cell lines (not just blood/lymphoid-adjacent like GM12878/E032/E062 above) -- the closest cell-type match this registry has found for any cohort, found via Martincorena et al. 2017's STAR Methods confirming dNdScv's own matrix is cell-line-based, which prompted checking ENCODE's classification=cell+line facet for a disease-matched line here.

ESCA.description: Esophageal Carcinoma. GTEx maps to Esophagus_Mucosa/Esophagus_Muscularis/Esophagus_Gastroesophageal_Junction; representative column is Mucosa (the epithelial layer, tumor cell-of-origin). Note the cohort itself mixes two genomically distinct histologies (squamous cell carcinoma and adenocarcinoma, the latter overlapping gastric/GEJ biology) -- a caveat for interpreting results, not something the covariate matrix can resolve. TCGA ATAC-seq covered (1 UUID, live-verified via GDC /data GET -- /files metadata 404s for this UUID the same way it does for CHOL's, a known GDC quirk, not a bad UUID). Roadmap uses E079 (Esophagus, the direct organ match, 6/7 marks -- H3K9ac 404s). No esophageal, gastric, or GI-tract cell line exists in ENCODE's Repli-seq experiment set or GEO GSE137764's MAT set (H1/H9/HCT116 only) -- repliseq is null, same as OV. encode_chromatin added 2026-09-03 (expanded-covariate-sources task, Objective A.4): adult primary esophagus (squamous epithelium) DNase-seq, filling the open-chromatin gap alongside the existing TCGA ATAC coverage.

GENERIC.description: Tissue-agnostic pan-tissue covariate pool, not a TCGA study code -- see sigmutselcovs' DEVELOPMENT.md, 'Generic (pan-tissue) covariates'. Objective B of the expanded-covariate-sources task (2026-09-03), rebuilt 2026-09-04 using the disk-bounded streaming download path (covariates_chromatin.py/download.py) after the original 26-EID plan hit gauss's disk limit. roadmap.eids is the full 127-epigenome Roadmap consolidated panel (E001-E129 excluding E060/E064, which genuinely don't exist -- verified live, not assumed); roadmap.marks adds DNase to the standard 7 histone marks, since Roadmap has its own native DNase-seq tracks via the same egg2.wustl.edu signal system for most EIDs (found while checking E121-E129's coverage), not just histone ChIP. encode_chromatin.tracks is 83 adult primary-tissue DNase-seq experiments from the ENCODE portal (one per unique biosample term, live-queried and life-stage-filtered to exclude embryonic/fetal/newborn/cell-line samples), complementing Roadmap's own DNase coverage with tissues Roadmap's panel doesn't reach. Still excludes H3K23ac/H3K14ac/H2AK9ac: no usable ENCODE coverage exists for any of the three (in-vitro-differentiated stem cells or one QC-flagged experiment only) -- unrelated to disk, a genuine data-availability gap. average_by_assay is true (2026-09-06): the raw per-track columns (roadmap's ~850 real tracks + encode_chromatin's 83) are pooled and collapsed to one averaged column per mark before assembly, rather than PCA-reduced as ~1860 separate per-track columns -- collapsing first cheaply outperforms PCA at the small component counts a per-cohort model can support, confirmed by 5-fold gene-CV against several TCGA cohorts' own covariate matrices. Cell lines added 2026-09-07: Martincorena et al. 2017's own STAR Methods (the primary paper, not just the dndscv package/GitHub repo, finally accessed this session) states plainly that dNdScv's 169-track/20-PC matrix came from '63 cell lines' in the Roadmap Epigenomics Project, not primary tissue -- a real, previously-unverified gap in GENERIC's own pool (which until now was 127 Roadmap epigenomes, mostly primary tissue/cells, plus 83 ENCODE adult-tissue DNase tracks, deliberately life-stage-filtered to EXCLUDE cell lines). Queried ENCODE's own portal restricted to biosample_ontology.classification=cell+line for all 7 default histone marks plus DNase (output_type 'fold change over control' for histone, 'read-depth normalized signal' for DNase, GRCh38): 211 distinct cell lines, 548 (line, mark) track pairs, zero overlap with GENERIC's existing 83 tissue-only DNase accessions. All 548 added here, unfiltered by tissue -- GENERIC is tissue-agnostic by design, so cell-line identity (unlike the per-cohort matrices' tissue-matching requirement) is not a rejection criterion here. Also added the 3 rare marks' full cell-line pool (H3K23ac/H3K14ac/H2AK9ac -- 7 biosamples: IMR-90, mesenchymal stem cell, H1, H9, trophoblast cell, neuronal stem cell, mesendoderm; 12 track pairs), the only place in this registry these 3 marks now appear at all, since no per-cohort tissue match exists for them (checked: IMR-90/H1/trophoblast/H9/mesenchymal-stem-cell/neuronal-stem-cell/mesendoderm match none of our 13 registered cohort tissues). average_by_assay's collapsing means this addition changes the resulting ~17-18 columns' underlying sample composition and precision, not their count -- consistent with why the mechanism was adopted in the first place (2026-09-06).
